named_confounds: genre composition shift (late period dominated by juvenile works)
sparse early-period sample (approx. 750 of 6766 works before 1876)
one passage per work, so rates are binary and noisy
date uncertainty (about half the works have low or medium date confidence)
rationale: Methods: 6766 works, each with one passage. The rate for each work is the DISTANCE_TRAVEL count divided by n_passages. I split works at year 1876 (late = year >= 1876), averaged works equally within each genre-by-period cell, took the late-minus-early difference for each genre, then averaged the 8 genres equally. Point estimate: +0.018 passage-rate units. A stratified bootstrap (2000 resamples within each genre-period cell) gives a 95% CI of [-0.006, 0.041], which includes zero. Genre results are mixed: juvenile, other and sensation_mystery rise; adventure, collection and domestic_realist fall slightly. Robustness checks: leaving out any one genre gives estimates from +0.010 to +0.023. Using only high-date-confidence works gives +0.031. Using only 1851-1899 gives +0.012. Raw decade means rise from about 0.05 to about 0.12, but that pooled trend mixes in the shift toward juvenile and adventure works. Every early cell is small (47-280 works), so precision is limited. Alternative explanations: changes in genre mix and sampling, dating errors near the cutoff, and annotation drift. The cited passages are labelled DISTANCE_TRAVEL and only illustrate the construct; they do not show a trend. The direction leans toward an increase, but the CI includes zero, so I abstain.
